bug_info.bug_desc: In spi_host_fsm.sv, sd_en_o is generated by a combinational mux that selects between a freshly computed value and a delayed copy, sd_en_ff_q. The selection depends on the current SPI clock level, sck_o, and on drive_posedge = (cpol != cpha). The intent was to update the data-line output enables only on the drive edge, but because sck_o is a level rather than a real edge and sd_en_ff_q lags by one clock, the output enable can reselect the stale registered value after the current enable has already changed or after cmd_wr_en_q has deasserted. This causes glitches or incorrect hold time on sd_en_o, so the output enables are not a clean function of the current segment direction, speed, and write-enable state. This violates the spec requirement that data-line output enables be controlled directly by the current transfer state and not depend on the instantaneous SPI clock phase or a delayed copy of the enable.
bug_info.fix_hint: Remove the sd_en_ff_q pipeline flops and the drive_posedge/sck_o qualification. Drive sd_en_o combinationally: when all chip-select outputs are high, force sd_en_o to zero; otherwise decode the current speed_o with cmd_wr_en_q (and cmd_wr_en_last_bit for Standard mode line 0 to hold the final bit drive) without falling back to a registered copy of sd_en_o.
